sections.title: The WHO bar: health is not merely the absence of disease

board_events.text: What does it actually mean to be HEALTHY?
Everyday usage: if nothing hurts, you are healthy. Health = absence of disease.
WHO: 'a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.'
All three dimensions AND the 'not merely' clause. A partial definition loses the mark.

board_events.text: Cricket team: eleven injury-free bodies still lose if confidence and teamwork have collapsed.
So a person free of every infection can still fail the WHO bar.
CBSE and CUET open with this as a 1-mark question. Certain marks — learn the line verbatim.

segments.text: <curious>Before we study what makes people ill, we have to be clear about what it means to be well. Let's start exactly where the chapter starts, and where the exam starts too.

In everyday speech, health is taken to mean simply the absence of disease. Nothing hurts, nothing is infected, so you are healthy. That is how all of us use the word — and it is precisely the answer the examiner is hoping you will give, so that you lose the mark.

The modern, exam-correct view is broader. The World Health Organization — spoken as W H O — defines health as a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.

Read that carefully, because there are four pieces in it, not one. Three dimensions — physical, mental, social — and then an explicit clarification that health is more than the absence of disease. Drop the social dimension, or drop that 'not merely' clause, and you have written a partial definition.

Here is the shape of it. Physical well-being, mental well-being, social well-being — three circles, and health sits only in the middle, where all three overlap. Notice what this picture refuses to allow: you cannot point at the physical circle alone and call it health.

Think about it this way. Picture a cricket team. Health is not just every player being injury-free — that is the physical part. It is also the players being confident and focused — that is mental. And it is them working together as a unit — that is social. A team can field eleven perfectly fit bodies and still play badly if morale or teamwork has collapsed.

The W H O is saying the human body is exactly like that team. Which gives us the conclusion the whole chapter rests on: a person can be free of any infection whatsoever and still not be healthy in the full sense, if they are mentally distressed or socially isolated. Not infected does not equal healthy.

<whisper>And this is among the cheapest marks in the entire syllabus. C B S E and C U E T open with this definition as a one-mark question almost every year. Learn the line word for word, and write all three dimensions plus the clarification.
<curious>बीमारी की बात करने से पहले हमें ये clear करना पड़ेगा कि well होने का मतलब क्या है। Chapter यहीं से शुरू होता है, और exam भी यहीं से शुरू होता है।

रोज़ की भाषा में health का मतलब लिया जाता है — absence of disease। कुछ दर्द नहीं हो रहा, कोई infection नहीं है, तो आप healthy हैं। हम सब यही मतलब लगाते हैं — और examiner को यही answer चाहिए, ताकि आपका mark कट जाए।

Modern और exam-correct view इससे कहीं ज़्यादा broad है। World Health Organization — बोलिए W H O — health को define करता है as a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity।

इसे ध्यान से पढ़िए, क्योंकि इसमें एक नहीं, चार pieces हैं। तीन dimensions — physical, mental, social — और उसके बाद एक explicit clarification कि health सिर्फ़ absence of disease नहीं है। Social dimension छोड़ दिया, या वो 'not merely' वाला clause छोड़ दिया, तो आपने अधूरी definition लिखी है।

इसकी shape देखिए। Physical well-being, mental well-being, social well-being — तीन circles, और health बैठता है बिल्कुल बीच में, जहाँ तीनों overlap करते हैं। ध्यान दीजिए ये picture क्या allow नहीं करती: आप अकेले physical circle को उंगली रखकर health नहीं कह सकते।

इसे ऐसे सोचिए। एक cricket team की कल्पना कीजिए। Health सिर्फ़ ये नहीं है कि हर player injury-free हो — वो physical part है। ये भी है कि players confident और focused हों — वो mental है। और वो एक unit की तरह मिलकर खेलें — वो social है। एक team ग्यारह बिल्कुल fit bodies उतार सकती है और फिर भी बुरा खेल सकती है, अगर morale या teamwork बिखर गया हो।

W H O यही कह रहा है कि human body बिल्कुल उस team जैसी है। और इससे वो conclusion निकलता है जिस पर पूरा chapter टिका है: कोई इंसान किसी भी infection से बिल्कुल free हो सकता है और फिर भी पूरे sense में healthy नहीं होगा, अगर वो mentally distressed है या socially isolated है। Not infected बराबर healthy नहीं होता।

<whisper>और ये पूरे syllabus के सबसे सस्ते marks में से है। C B S E और C U E T लगभग हर साल इस definition को one mark question की तरह पूछते हैं। Line को word for word याद कीजिए, और तीनों dimensions के साथ clarification भी लिखिए।

sections.title: Disease, and the three things that decide your health

board_events.text: DISEASE = normal functioning breaks down, and the body announces it
Disease: any condition in which the functioning of one or more organs or systems of the body is adversely affected.
Marked by recognisable SIGNS and SYMPTOMS — the announcement is part of the definition.

board_events.text: What determines health? Three broad influences: GENETIC · INFECTIONS · LIFESTYLE.
Genetic — deficiencies a child is born with, inherited from the parents.
Infections — by the pathogens studied through this chapter. Lifestyle — food, water, rest, exercise, habits.
Health can be actively BUILT: balanced diet, hygiene, exercise, awareness, immunisation.
Good health raises productivity and life expectancy, and cuts infant and maternal mortality — a national priority, not just a personal one.

segments.text: We have defined the well side. Now define the other side properly, because 'disease' also has a technical definition and it is not just 'feeling bad'.

A disease is any condition in which the functioning of one or more organs or systems of the body is adversely affected. Hold on to the word functioning. It is not about pain, it is not about how you feel — it is about a job not being done.

And there is a second half to the definition: the condition is marked by recognisable signs and symptoms. The moment normal functioning breaks down and the body signals that breakdown, we say a disease is present. The announcement is part of the definition, not an optional extra.

So on the left of the board, organs and systems each doing their job, nothing being reported. On the right, one or more of them adversely affected, and recognisable signs and symptoms appearing. The arrow between them is the breakdown — and the rest of this chapter is a study of what pushes you across that arrow.

So what decides which side you sit on? The chapter names three broad influences, and they are worth memorising as a set of three because that is exactly how they are asked. Genetic disorders, infections, and lifestyle.

Genetic disorders first — these are deficiencies a child is born with, inherited from the parents. You did not catch them and you did not choose them. Sickle-cell anaemia is the standard example, and we will meet it again in a rather surprising place later in this part.

Infections second — caused by the pathogens we study through this whole chapter, and the reason the next subtopic is as long as it is. And lifestyle third — the food and water we consume, our rest and exercise, our habits and routines. Notice that of the three, this is the one entirely inside your control.

<excited>And here is the optimistic half, which students skip and examiners ask. Health can be actively built and protected. A balanced diet. Personal and public hygiene. Regular exercise. Awareness. And large-scale vaccination and immunisation programmes, which have eradicated or controlled once-deadly diseases.

Good health, in turn, raises productivity, lengthens life expectancy, and reduces infant and maternal mortality. That is why health is treated as a national priority and not merely a personal one — and that sentence is a ready-made closing line for any long-answer question in this section.
Well वाला side हमने define कर लिया। अब दूसरे side को भी properly define कीजिए, क्योंकि disease की भी एक technical definition है और वो सिर्फ़ 'बुरा लगना' नहीं है।

Disease वो condition है जिसमें body के एक या ज़्यादा organs या systems की functioning adversely affected हो जाती है। Functioning शब्द को पकड़ के रखिए। ये pain की बात नहीं है, ये feeling की बात नहीं है — ये इस बात की बात है कि कोई काम नहीं हो रहा।

और definition का एक दूसरा half भी है: ये condition recognisable signs और symptoms से marked होती है। जिस moment normal functioning टूटती है और body उस breakdown का signal देती है, हम कहते हैं disease present है। Announcement definition का हिस्सा है, कोई optional extra नहीं।

तो board के left पर — organs और systems सब अपना-अपना काम कर रहे हैं, कुछ report नहीं हो रहा। Right पर — इनमें से एक या ज़्यादा adversely affected, और recognisable signs और symptoms आ गए। बीच का arrow ही breakdown है — और बाकी पूरा chapter इसी की study है कि आपको उस arrow के पार क्या धकेलता है।

तो ये decide कौन करता है कि आप किस side बैठेंगे? Chapter तीन broad influences गिनाता है, और इन्हें एक set of three की तरह याद कीजिए क्योंकि exactly ऐसे ही पूछे जाते हैं। Genetic disorders, infections, और lifestyle।

पहले genetic disorders — ये वो deficiencies हैं जो बच्चा जन्म से लेकर आता है, parents से inherited। न आपने इन्हें catch किया, न choose किया। Sickle-cell anaemia standard example है, और इसी part में आगे हम इससे एक बड़ी surprising जगह पर दोबारा मिलेंगे।

दूसरा infections — ये उन pathogens से होते हैं जिनकी study पूरा chapter करता है, और यही वजह है कि अगला subtopic इतना लंबा है। तीसरा lifestyle — हमारा खाना और पानी, rest और exercise, habits और routines। ध्यान दीजिए तीनों में से यही एक पूरी तरह आपके control में है।

<excited>और अब optimistic half, जिसे students skip कर देते हैं और examiners पूछ लेते हैं। Health को actively build और protect किया जा सकता है। Balanced diet। Personal और public hygiene। Regular exercise। Awareness। और large-scale vaccination और immunisation programmes, जिन्होंने कभी की deadly diseases को eradicate या control कर दिया।

और अच्छी health बदले में productivity बढ़ाती है, life expectancy लंबी करती है, और infant तथा maternal mortality घटाती है। इसीलिए health को national priority माना जाता है, सिर्फ़ personal नहीं — और ये line इस section के किसी भी long-answer का ready-made closing बन जाती है।

sections.title: Four words the rest of the chapter assumes

board_events.text: The vocabulary everything later depends on
PATHOGEN — any disease-causing organism: bacterium, virus, fungus, protozoan, or worm (helminth).
VECTOR — an organism that transmits a pathogen WITHOUT itself causing the disease.

board_events.text: INFECTIOUS = communicable — spreads from person to person.
NON-INFECTIOUS = non-communicable — does not spread between people.
The vector carries but never suffers. Anopheles carries malaria; she does not 'have' malaria the way we do.
Get these four right and the disease tables in the next subtopic stop being a memory exercise.

segments.text: Four words now. They look like simple definitions, and they are — but every table, every match-the-column and every mechanism in the next fifty minutes assumes you already own them.

A pathogen is any disease-causing organism. Note the width of that: a bacterium, a virus, a fungus, a protozoan, or a worm — a helminth. Five kinds, and the next subtopic is organised into exactly those five columns. Pathogen is not a synonym for bacterium.

A vector is an organism that transmits a pathogen without itself causing the disease. That second half is the whole point of the word. If the organism causes the disease, it is the pathogen. If it only moves the pathogen around, it is the vector.

On the board: pathogen at the top in red, because it does the harm. Vector in green below it, because it does the ferrying. And underneath, the split that organises the entire chapter — infectious against non-infectious.

Infectious, also called communicable, means the disease spreads from person to person. Someone else's illness can become yours. That is what the word is doing — it is a statement about transmissibility, not about severity.

Non-infectious, also called non-communicable, means the disease does not spread between people. And notice that this says nothing about how dangerous it is. Cancer is non-infectious and it is the single most important non-infectious cause of death. Non-communicable does not mean mild.

<curious>Here is the line worth carrying out of this section. The vector carries but never suffers. The female Anopheles mosquito carries malaria — she does not have malaria in the sense that we do. She is the courier, not the criminal, and the exam will test whether you can hold that distinction.

Get these four words right and the disease tables in the next subtopic stop being a memory exercise and start being a system. Every row is just: which pathogen, which vector if any, does it spread. Same three slots, filled differently.
अब चार शब्द। दिखने में simple definitions हैं, और हैं भी — लेकिन अगले पचास मिनट की हर table, हर match-the-column और हर mechanism ये मानकर चलता है कि ये चार आपको आते हैं।

Pathogen कोई भी disease-causing organism है। इस width पर ध्यान दीजिए: bacterium, virus, fungus, protozoan, या worm — यानी helminth। पाँच kinds, और अगला subtopic exactly इन्हीं पाँच columns में organise किया गया है। Pathogen का मतलब bacterium नहीं होता।

Vector वो organism है जो pathogen को transmit करता है, बिना ख़ुद disease cause किए। वो दूसरा half ही इस word का पूरा point है। अगर organism disease cause करता है, वो pathogen है। अगर वो सिर्फ़ pathogen को इधर से उधर ले जाता है, वो vector है।

Board पर देखिए: pathogen सबसे ऊपर red में, क्योंकि नुक़सान वही करता है। नीचे vector green में, क्योंकि ferrying वो करता है। और सबसे नीचे वो split जो पूरे chapter को organise करता है — infectious versus non-infectious।
Infectious, जिसे communicable भी कहते हैं, मतलब disease person to person फैलती है। किसी और की बीमारी आपकी बन सकती है। बस यही कह रहा है ये word — ये transmissibility का statement है, severity का नहीं।

Non-infectious, यानी non-communicable, मतलब disease लोगों के बीच फैलती नहीं। और ध्यान दीजिए, ये इस बारे में कुछ नहीं कहता कि वो कितनी ख़तरनाक है। Cancer non-infectious है और वही सबसे बड़ी non-infectious cause of death है। Non-communicable का मतलब mild नहीं होता।

<curious>अब वो line जो इस section से लेकर जाइए। Vector carries but never suffers. Female Anopheles mosquito malaria को carry करती है — उसे malaria उस sense में नहीं है जिस sense में हमें होता है। वो courier है, criminal नहीं, और exam यही test करेगा कि आप ये distinction पकड़ पाते हैं या नहीं।

ये चार words सही कर लीजिए और अगले subtopic की disease tables memory exercise होना बंद करके एक system बन जाएँगी। हर row बस इतनी है: कौन सा pathogen, vector है तो कौन सा, और क्या ये फैलती है। वही तीन slots, अलग-अलग भरे हुए।

sections.title: The master classification tree: can it spread?

board_events.text: The first question to ask about ANY disease named in an exam
Ask: can it spread from person to person? That one question routes you to the right body of knowledge.

board_events.caption: The master tree — infectious vs non-infectious, and what hangs under each

board_events.text: INFECTIOUS — caused by pathogens, transmissible. Grouped by pathogen type: bacterial, viral, protozoan, helminthic, fungal.
NON-INFECTIOUS — not transmissible. Genetic/congenital · degenerative/lifestyle · cancer · substance-abuse disorders.
Genetic/congenital: present from birth, e.g. sickle-cell anaemia. Degenerative/lifestyle: heart disease, diabetes.
CANCER is the leading non-infectious cause of death — and it is the reason 'disease' must never be read as 'infection'.
The branches are not decoration: infectious → subtopic 01; cancer → subtopic 02; substance abuse → subtopic 03.

segments.text: This is the tree the whole chapter hangs on, and I want you to build the habit of walking it before you answer anything. Any disease name lands in front of you in an exam — malaria, cancer, ringworm, whatever it is — you ask one question first.

Can it spread from person to person? That single question splits the entire subject in half and routes you to the right body of knowledge. Answer it before you try to recall symptoms or organisms, because the two halves behave completely differently.
Here is the tree. Disease at the top, that one question underneath it, and then two branches that never mix. Everything else in this chapter is filed under one branch or the other.

Say yes, it spreads. Then it is infectious — also called communicable — and by definition it is caused by a pathogen and is transmissible. And now a second question opens up, which is: what kind of pathogen? Bacterial, viral, protozoan, helminthic, or fungal. Those five sub-branches are literally the structure of our next subtopic.

Say no, it does not spread. Then it is non-infectious, non-communicable, and there is no organism to name at all. Under this branch sit the genetic or congenital diseases, the degenerative and lifestyle diseases, cancer, and the disorders linked to substance abuse.

Take those in turn. Genetic or congenital means present from birth — sickle-cell anaemia is the example the chapter gives. Degenerative or lifestyle means it develops from how you live — heart disease and diabetes. Nobody caught either of them from anybody.

<whisper>And then cancer, which I have written in red for a reason. Cancer is the leading non-infectious cause of death. That is exactly why the word disease must never be read as infection — the biggest killer on this tree has no pathogen at all, no vector, and nothing to catch.

Last thing, and it makes this diagram worth more than it looks. These branches are not decoration — they are a map of the chapter. The infectious branch is subtopic zero one. Cancer sits in subtopic zero two, next to immunity. Substance abuse is subtopic zero three. You are looking at the table of contents.

यही वो tree है जिस पर पूरा chapter टिका है, और मैं चाहता हूँ कि आप कुछ भी answer करने से पहले इस पर चलने की आदत बना लें। Exam में कोई भी disease का नाम सामने आए — malaria, cancer, ringworm, जो भी हो — आप पहले एक सवाल पूछिए।

क्या ये person to person फैल सकती है? यही अकेला सवाल पूरे subject को दो हिस्सों में काट देता है और आपको सही knowledge तक भेज देता है। Symptoms या organism याद करने की कोशिश से पहले इसे answer कीजिए, क्योंकि दोनों halves बिल्कुल अलग तरह से behave करते हैं।
ये रहा tree। सबसे ऊपर disease, उसके नीचे वो एक सवाल, और फिर दो branches जो कभी आपस में नहीं मिलतीं। इस chapter की बाक़ी हर चीज़ इन्हीं में से एक branch के नीचे file होती है।

मान लीजिए जवाब है हाँ, फैलती है। तो वो infectious है — communicable भी कहते हैं — और definition से ही वो pathogen से होती है और transmissible है। और अब दूसरा सवाल खुलता है: कौन से kind का pathogen? Bacterial, viral, protozoan, helminthic, या fungal। यही पाँच sub-branches literally हमारे अगले subtopic का structure हैं।

अब मान लीजिए जवाब है नहीं, फैलती नहीं। तो वो non-infectious है, non-communicable, और यहाँ नाम लेने के लिए कोई organism है ही नहीं। इस branch के नीचे आती हैं genetic या congenital diseases, degenerative और lifestyle diseases, cancer, और substance abuse से जुड़े disorders।

एक-एक करके देखिए। Genetic या congenital मतलब जन्म से present — sickle-cell anaemia वो example है जो chapter देता है। Degenerative या lifestyle मतलब आपके जीने के तरीक़े से बनी — heart disease और diabetes। इनमें से कोई भी किसी ने किसी से पकड़ी नहीं।

<whisper>और फिर cancer, जिसे मैंने वजह से red में लिखा है। Cancer leading non-infectious cause of death है। यही तो exactly वजह है कि disease शब्द को कभी infection नहीं पढ़ना चाहिए — इस tree का सबसे बड़ा killer, जिसका कोई pathogen नहीं, कोई vector नहीं, और पकड़ने को कुछ नहीं।

आख़िरी बात, और इसी से ये diagram दिखने से ज़्यादा क़ीमती हो जाती है। ये branches decoration नहीं हैं — ये chapter का map हैं। Infectious branch है subtopic zero one। Cancer बैठा है subtopic zero two में, immunity के साथ। Substance abuse है subtopic zero three। आप table of contents देख रहे हैं।

board_events.text: 1. BALANCED NUTRITION — adequate, clean food and safe drinking water keep defences and repair systems supplied.
2. HYGIENE — personal blocks entry at the individual; public protects the whole community.
3. AWARENESS AND LIFESTYLE — exercise, rest, and informed choices prevent the large non-infectious burden.
4. IMMUNISATION — trains the population's immune memory in advance; drove the control of smallpox and polio.
Public hygiene = disposal of waste and excreta, periodic cleaning of water reservoirs, vector control.
Hygiene → subtopic 01 · Immunisation → subtopic 02 · Avoiding abuse → subtopic 03. The introduction IS the map.

segments.text: One reframing before we leave this subtopic, and it is the one that turns a boring introduction into something worth your time. Health is not a static state that you either have or lack.

It is a balance, actively maintained, against constant microbial and lifestyle pressure. Nothing about it is passive. And the chapter gives us four practical levers that do the maintaining — four, and they are asked as a set.

Here they are on the left, and on the right I have done something the textbook only hints at: I have shown you where each one reappears later. Watch that column, because it is the reason this section exists.

Lever one, balanced nutrition. Adequate, clean food and safe drinking water keep the body's defences and repair systems supplied. Not glamorous, but notice the word defences — your immune system is built out of what you eat, so nutrition is upstream of everything in subtopic zero two.

Lever two, hygiene, and this splits into two halves that get confused constantly. Personal hygiene — a clean body, safe food and water — blocks pathogen entry at the individual level. Public hygiene protects the whole community: proper disposal of waste and excreta, periodic cleaning of water reservoirs, and vector control.

Lever three, awareness and lifestyle. Regular exercise, adequate rest, and informed choices — avoiding tobacco, alcohol and drug abuse. This lever is what prevents that entire large non-infectious burden sitting on the right branch of the tree we just drew.

Lever four, immunisation. Vaccination programmes train the population's immune memory in advance, and they have driven the control or eradication of diseases such as smallpox and polio. Note what that sentence quietly claims — the biology is coming in subtopic zero two, but the result is already historical fact.

Now hold on to that public hygiene definition, because it is a favourite short answer. Disposal of waste and excreta. Periodic cleaning of water reservoirs. Vector control. Three items — and every one of them will reappear as a control measure in the very next subtopic.

<excited>And here is the payoff. Look at how each lever maps onto a later section. Hygiene and vector control point at the infectious diseases of subtopic zero one. Immunisation points at the immunity of subtopic zero two. Avoiding substance abuse points at subtopic zero three. The introduction is not a warm-up — it is the map of the whole chapter.
इस subtopic को छोड़ने से पहले एक reframing, और यही वो चीज़ है जो एक boring introduction को आपके time के लायक़ बना देती है। Health कोई static state नहीं है जो या तो आपके पास है या नहीं है।

ये एक balance है, जो actively maintain किया जाता है, लगातार चलते microbial और lifestyle pressure के ख़िलाफ़। इसमें कुछ भी passive नहीं है। और chapter हमें चार practical levers देता है जो ये maintenance करते हैं — चार, और ये एक set की तरह पूछे जाते हैं।

ये रहे left में, और right में मैंने वो कर दिया है जिसका textbook सिर्फ़ इशारा करता है: मैंने दिखा दिया है कि हर lever आगे कहाँ दोबारा आता है। उस column पर नज़र रखिए, क्योंकि यही इस section के होने की वजह है।

Lever एक, balanced nutrition। पर्याप्त, clean food और safe drinking water body की defences और repair systems को supplied रखते हैं। Glamorous नहीं है, लेकिन defences शब्द पर ध्यान दीजिए — आपका immune system उसी से बनता है जो आप खाते हैं, तो nutrition subtopic zero two की हर चीज़ से upstream है।

Lever दो, hygiene, और ये दो halves में बँटता है जिन्हें students लगातार गड्डमड्ड करते हैं। Personal hygiene — साफ़ शरीर, safe food और water — individual level पर pathogen की entry रोकती है। Public hygiene पूरी community को बचाती है: waste और excreta का proper disposal, water reservoirs की periodic cleaning, और vector control।

Lever तीन, awareness और lifestyle। Regular exercise, पर्याप्त rest, और informed choices — tobacco, alcohol और drug abuse से बचना। यही lever उस पूरे बड़े non-infectious burden को रोकता है जो अभी बनाए tree की right branch पर बैठा था।

Lever चार, immunisation। Vaccination programmes पूरी population की immune memory को पहले से train कर देते हैं, और इन्होंने smallpox और polio जैसी बीमारियों को control या eradicate किया है। ध्यान दीजिए ये line चुपचाप क्या claim कर रही है — biology subtopic zero two में आएगी, लेकिन result पहले से historical fact है।

अब उस public hygiene वाली definition को पकड़े रखिए, क्योंकि ये favourite short answer है। Waste और excreta का disposal। Water reservoirs की periodic cleaning। Vector control। तीन items — और इनमें से हर एक बिल्कुल अगले subtopic में control measure बनकर लौटेगा।

<excited>और अब payoff। देखिए हर lever आगे किस section पर जाकर बैठता है। Hygiene और vector control इशारा करते हैं subtopic zero one की infectious diseases पर। Immunisation इशारा करता है subtopic zero two की immunity पर। Substance abuse से बचना इशारा करता है subtopic zero three पर। Introduction कोई warm-up नहीं है — ये पूरे chapter का map है।

board_events.text: Q1 [CBSE] Define health as given by the World Health Organization.
Answer: 'a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.'
Full marks needs BOTH: all three dimensions, AND the clarification that it is more than the absence of disease.

board_events.text: Infectious: (i) malaria and (iii) typhoid — both caused by transmissible pathogens.
Non-infectious: (ii) cancer — lifestyle/genetic, the leading non-infectious cause of death; (iv) sickle-cell anaemia — genetic/congenital.
Answer: A-infectious, B-non-infectious, C-infectious, D-non-infectious. State the REASON for each — that is where the marks sit.

segments.text: Two questions, and they are the two the board actually asks from this subtopic. The first one looks free. It is not quite free, and I will show you where students drop the mark.

Question one, from C B S E: define health as given by the World Health Organization. Answer: health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity. That is it. That is the whole answer.

But here is the mark scheme. Full marks needs both halves: all three dimensions — physical, mental and social — and the clarification that it is more than the absence of disease. Students write the three dimensions, stop, and feel confident. The 'not merely' clause is doing real work in that sentence and the examiner is checking for it.
Question two, from C U E T. Classify the following as infectious or non-infectious: malaria, cancer, typhoid, and sickle-cell anaemia.
Do not reach for symptoms. Walk the tree. Ask of each one, in order: can this spread from person to person? That is the only question, and it decides all four in about ten seconds.
Here is the sorting. Two go left, two go right, and I have written the reason under each name — because in a classify question the reason is what is actually being marked.

Malaria and typhoid go into infectious. Both are caused by transmissible pathogens. Malaria is protozoan and comes to you through a mosquito; typhoid is bacterial and comes through contaminated food and water. Different pathogen, different route, same verdict — someone else's illness can become yours.

Cancer and sickle-cell anaemia go into non-infectious. Cancer is lifestyle and genetic in origin, and remember it is the leading non-infectious cause of death — the biggest killer here and still nothing to catch. Sickle-cell anaemia is genetic and congenital, present from birth, inherited from the parents.

<whisper>So the answer is: malaria infectious, cancer non-infectious, typhoid infectious, sickle-cell anaemia non-infectious. And write the reason beside each one, even when the question does not explicitly ask for it. In a classify question, the label is half a mark and the justification is the other half.
दो सवाल, और यही दो हैं जो board इस subtopic से actually पूछता है। पहला मुफ़्त लगता है। बिल्कुल मुफ़्त नहीं है, और मैं दिखाता हूँ students mark कहाँ गँवाते हैं।

सवाल एक, C B S E से: World Health Organization के अनुसार health को define कीजिए। Answer: health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity। बस। पूरा answer यही है।

लेकिन mark scheme सुनिए। Full marks के लिए दोनों halves चाहिए: तीनों dimensions — physical, mental और social — और वो clarification कि ये absence of disease से ज़्यादा है। Students तीन dimensions लिखकर रुक जाते हैं और confident महसूस करते हैं। वो 'not merely' वाला clause उस sentence में असली काम कर रहा है और examiner उसी को check कर रहा है।
सवाल दो, C U E T से। इन्हें infectious या non-infectious में classify कीजिए: malaria, cancer, typhoid, और sickle-cell anaemia।
Symptoms की तरफ़ मत भागिए। Tree पर चलिए। हर एक से बारी-बारी पूछिए: क्या ये person to person फैल सकती है? बस यही सवाल है, और यही चारों को क़रीब दस सेकंड में decide कर देता है।
ये रही sorting। दो left गईं, दो right, और मैंने हर नाम के नीचे reason लिख दिया है — क्योंकि classify वाले सवाल में असल में marks reason के ही मिलते हैं।

Malaria और typhoid infectious में जाएँगी। दोनों transmissible pathogens से होती हैं। Malaria protozoan है और mosquito के ज़रिए आती है; typhoid bacterial है और contaminated food तथा water से आती है। अलग pathogen, अलग route, वही verdict — किसी और की बीमारी आपकी बन सकती है।

Cancer और sickle-cell anaemia non-infectious में जाएँगी। Cancer का origin lifestyle और genetic है, और याद रखिए ये leading non-infectious cause of death है — यहाँ का सबसे बड़ा killer, और फिर भी पकड़ने को कुछ नहीं। Sickle-cell anaemia genetic और congenital है, जन्म से present, parents से inherited।

<whisper>तो answer है: malaria infectious, cancer non-infectious, typhoid infectious, sickle-cell anaemia non-infectious। और हर एक के बग़ल में reason लिखिए, चाहे सवाल ने explicitly न भी माँगा हो। Classify वाले सवाल में label आधा mark है और justification बाक़ी आधा।

sections.title: Pitfalls: the two equations that are not equations

board_events.text: Two traps live in this subtopic — and both are equals signs that should not exist
TRAP 1: 'not infected' = 'healthy'. FALSE.
The WHO definition deliberately includes the mental and social dimensions. Infection-free is one third of the bar.
TRAP 2: 'disease' = 'something you catch'. FALSE.
A large class is non-infectious — genetic, lifestyle, degenerative — and the leading non-infectious cause of death is CANCER.
One-liner for the margin: 'No germ is not the same as healthy.' The WHO bar is physical PLUS mental PLUS social.
In MCQs, options offering 'absence of disease' or 'freedom from infection' as the WHO definition are the designed trap — they are the everyday usage.
'Immunity' is a contributor to health, not the definition of it. That distractor appears too.

segments.text: Short section, two traps, and both of them are the same mistake wearing different clothes. Both are equals signs that students write without noticing, and that this subtopic exists specifically to break.
Trap one. Not infected equals healthy. That is false, and the whole first section was an argument against it.

The W H O definition deliberately includes the mental and social dimensions. Being infection-free clears the physical bar and nothing else — roughly one third of the definition. A person with no pathogen anywhere in them, who is mentally distressed or socially isolated, is not healthy by the definition you are being examined on. Do not equate not infected with healthy.
Trap two, which is the mirror image. Disease equals something you catch. Also false.

A large class of disease is non-infectious — genetic, lifestyle, degenerative. Nothing was caught from anybody. And the single most important non-infectious cause of death is cancer, which tells you how big this supposedly secondary branch actually is. If you read the word disease and your mind goes straight to germs, you have already lost half the chapter.
So write this in your margin, because it compresses both traps into one line. No germ is not the same as healthy. The W H O bar is physical plus mental plus social — all three, every time.

<whisper>Now the exam application, because both traps are weaponised the same way. In a multiple-choice question asking for the W H O definition, you will be offered 'the absence of disease' and 'freedom from infection' as options. Those are not careless wrong answers. They are the everyday usage, planted deliberately, because they feel right.

And one more distractor to know by sight: 'the presence of strong immunity'. Immunity is a contributor to health, not the definition of it — and this option catches good students precisely because they know immunity matters. Read what the question asked. It asked for a definition.
छोटा section, दो traps, और दोनों दरअसल एक ही ग़लती हैं अलग कपड़ों में। दोनों ऐसे equals signs हैं जो students बिना ध्यान दिए लिख देते हैं, और ये subtopic specifically इन्हीं को तोड़ने के लिए है।
Trap एक। Not infected बराबर healthy। ये ग़लत है, और पूरा पहला section इसी के ख़िलाफ़ एक argument था।

W H O की definition जान-बूझकर mental और social dimensions शामिल करती है। Infection-free होना सिर्फ़ physical bar पार करता है और कुछ नहीं — मोटे तौर पर definition का एक तिहाई। जिस इंसान के अंदर कहीं कोई pathogen नहीं है लेकिन वो mentally distressed या socially isolated है, वो उस definition से healthy नहीं है जिस पर आपका exam हो रहा है। Not infected को healthy मत मानिए।
Trap दो, जो इसी का mirror image है। Disease बराबर कुछ जो आप पकड़ते हैं। ये भी ग़लत।

Disease का एक बड़ा class non-infectious है — genetic, lifestyle, degenerative। किसी से कुछ पकड़ा ही नहीं गया। और सबसे बड़ी single non-infectious cause of death है cancer, जिससे आपको पता चलता है कि ये तथाकथित secondary branch असल में कितनी बड़ी है। अगर disease शब्द पढ़ते ही आपका दिमाग़ सीधे germs पर जाता है, तो आधा chapter आप पहले ही गँवा चुके हैं।
तो ये margin में लिख लीजिए, क्योंकि ये दोनों traps को एक line में compress कर देता है। No germ is not the same as healthy। W H O का bar है physical plus mental plus social — तीनों, हर बार।

<whisper>अब exam application, क्योंकि दोनों traps को एक ही तरीक़े से हथियार बनाया जाता है। W H O की definition पूछने वाले multiple-choice में आपको options मिलेंगे — 'the absence of disease' और 'freedom from infection'। ये लापरवाही से बने ग़लत answers नहीं हैं। ये रोज़ की भाषा है, जान-बूझकर रखी गई, क्योंकि ये सही महसूस होती है।

और एक distractor देखते ही पहचान लीजिए: 'the presence of strong immunity'। Immunity health में contribute करती है, वो health की definition नहीं है — और ये option अच्छे students को exactly इसलिए पकड़ता है क्योंकि उन्हें पता है immunity मायने रखती है। सवाल ने जो पूछा वो पढ़िए। उसने definition पूछी थी।

sections.title: The walled city: two families of disease, and the invader

board_events.text: Two broad families — and only one of them has an invader
NON-INFECTIOUS — cancer, diabetes, most genetic disorders. Arise from WITHIN. Do not jump person to person.
INFECTIOUS — caused by an invader: a living organism that gets inside and disrupts things. These SPREAD.

board_events.text: Also called communicable or transmissible diseases — because they spread.
The invader has a name: a PATHOGEN — bacterium, virus, fungus, protozoan, or worm (helminth).
Crucially: most pathogens are PARASITES. They harm the host simply by living in or on it.
Stealing resources and damaging tissue is a BY-PRODUCT of their own survival — not a purpose.

segments.text: <curious>Imagine your body as a walled city. Most of the time the gates hold, trade flows, and life is ordinary. A disease is what happens when that ordinary functioning breaks down — when one or more organs stop doing their job properly, and the body announces the trouble through signs and symptoms.

And diseases come in two broad families, which is the split we drew in the last subtopic — now with a picture attached. Non-infectious diseases — cancer, diabetes, most genetic disorders — arise from within the city. Nothing came through the gate. And they do not jump from person to person.

Infectious diseases, which are our concern for the rest of this part, are caused by an invader. A living organism that gets inside the city walls and disrupts things. And because there is an invader, and invaders can move, these diseases spread.

Look at the two panels. On the left the walls are intact and the breakdown still happened — that is non-infectious. On the right something came over the wall. Same outcome, completely different story, and everything you need to know about a disease follows from which panel it belongs in.

Because they spread, these are also called communicable or transmissible diseases. Three words for one property. If a question uses any of them, it is telling you there is an organism involved, and it is telling you the disease can be passed on.

And that invader has a name: a pathogen. We defined it last subtopic and here it is doing real work. A pathogen is any disease-causing organism — a bacterium, a virus, a fungus, a protozoan, or a worm, which is a helminth. Five kinds. The entire disease table of this subtopic is those five kinds, one column each.
Now here is the sentence that changes how you think about all of this. Most pathogens are parasites. They harm the host simply by living in or on it.

Sit with that for a second, because it corrects the war metaphor I just gave you. The bacterium is not attacking you. It is not trying to make you ill. It is eating, growing and reproducing — and stealing your resources and damaging your tissue is a by-product of its own survival, not a purpose. Your symptoms are collateral. That is what a parasite is.

<curious>अपनी body को एक walled city की तरह imagine कीजिए। ज़्यादातर वक़्त gates टिके रहते हैं, trade चलता है, ज़िंदगी सामान्य रहती है। Disease तब होती है जब वो सामान्य functioning टूटती है — जब एक या ज़्यादा organs ठीक से अपना काम करना बंद कर देते हैं, और body signs तथा symptoms के ज़रिए इस मुसीबत का ऐलान करती है।

और diseases दो broad families में आती हैं, यानी वही split जो हमने पिछले subtopic में बनाया था — अब picture के साथ। Non-infectious diseases — cancer, diabetes, ज़्यादातर genetic disorders — city के अंदर से ही उठती हैं। Gate से कुछ नहीं आया। और ये person to person कूदती नहीं।

Infectious diseases, जो इस पूरे part में हमारा concern हैं, एक invader से होती हैं। एक living organism जो city walls के अंदर घुस जाता है और सब गड़बड़ कर देता है। और चूँकि एक invader है, और invaders चल सकते हैं, इसलिए ये diseases फैलती हैं।

दोनों panels देखिए। Left में walls सही-सलामत हैं और फिर भी breakdown हुआ — वो non-infectious है। Right में कुछ दीवार लाँघकर आया। नतीजा वही, कहानी बिल्कुल अलग — और किसी disease के बारे में आपको जो कुछ जानना है वो इसी से निकलता है कि वो किस panel की है।

फैलने की वजह से इन्हें communicable या transmissible diseases भी कहते हैं। एक property के लिए तीन शब्द। अगर सवाल इनमें से कोई भी शब्द use करता है, तो वो आपको बता रहा है कि यहाँ कोई organism है, और वो बता रहा है कि ये disease आगे पहुँच सकती है।

और उस invader का एक नाम है: pathogen। पिछले subtopic में define किया था और यहाँ वो असली काम कर रहा है। Pathogen कोई भी disease-causing organism है — bacterium, virus, fungus, protozoan, या worm यानी helminth। पाँच kinds। इस subtopic की पूरी disease table यही पाँच kinds हैं, हर एक का एक column।
अब वो sentence जो इस सब के बारे में आपकी सोच बदल देगी। ज़्यादातर pathogens parasites होते हैं। वो host को सिर्फ़ उसके अंदर या ऊपर रहकर ही नुक़सान पहुँचाते हैं।

एक second इस पर रुकिए, क्योंकि ये उस war metaphor को correct कर देता है जो मैंने अभी दिया। Bacterium आप पर हमला नहीं कर रहा। वो आपको बीमार करने की कोशिश नहीं कर रहा। वो खा रहा है, बढ़ रहा है, reproduce कर रहा है — और आपके resources चुराना तथा आपकी tissue damage करना उसके अपने survival का by-product है, मक़सद नहीं। आपके symptoms collateral हैं। Parasite यही होता है।

sections.title: Host, pathogen, vector — the three anchors

board_events.text: Three ideas anchor this whole subtopic. Fix them now.
HOST — the organism the pathogen lives in (us).
PATHOGEN — the organism that causes the disease.
VECTOR — the organism that transports the pathogen. No disease of its own.

board_events.text: Festival railway rush: the troublemaker sometimes walks in directly — you inhale a cough droplet.
Sometimes he cannot make the journey alone and needs a courier — a train, a ticket. That courier is the vector, very often an insect.
The female Anopheles is the classic vector: she carries malaria but does not 'have' malaria in the sense that we do.

segments.text: Three ideas anchor this whole subtopic, and I want them fixed before a single disease name arrives, because every table that follows is these three slots filled differently.

The host is the organism the pathogen lives in. In this chapter, that is us. Not a complicated idea — but notice it is defined by being lived in, not by being ill. That distinction is going to matter in about two minutes.

The pathogen is the organism that causes the disease. It is the one doing the damage. When a question says 'name the causative organism', it is asking for the pathogen, and nothing else on this board is an acceptable answer.
And the vector is the organism that transports the pathogen — and it has no disease of its own. That last clause is the entire content of the word. Take it away and vector just means pathogen.

Here is the triangle. Pathogen at the top in red because it harms. Host bottom left, that is us. Vector bottom right in green, with a dashed arrow running across the bottom — because the vector's whole job is that arrow, delivering the pathogen from a sick person to a healthy one.

Think about it this way. Picture the Indian railway network during a festival rush. The pathogen is the troublemaker who wants to reach a distant town. Sometimes the troublemaker walks in directly — you inhale a cough droplet and the pathogen has made its own journey. No help needed.

But sometimes he cannot make the journey alone and needs a carrier — a train, a ticket, a courier. That courier is the vector: an organism, very often an insect, that does not cause the disease itself but ferries the pathogen from a sick person to a healthy one. It is transport, and nothing more.

<whisper>And the classic vector is the female Anopheles mosquito. She carries malaria — but she does not have malaria in the sense that we do. She is a healthy courier. When an exam asks whether the mosquito is the pathogen or the vector, this is the distinction being tested, and it is worth a mark every single year.
तीन ideas इस पूरे subtopic को anchor करते हैं, और मैं चाहता हूँ ये एक भी disease का नाम आने से पहले fix हो जाएँ, क्योंकि आगे की हर table यही तीन slots हैं, बस अलग-अलग भरे हुए।

Host वो organism है जिसमें pathogen रहता है। इस chapter में वो हम हैं। कोई मुश्किल idea नहीं — लेकिन ध्यान दीजिए ये define इस बात से होता है कि उसमें कोई रह रहा है, इस बात से नहीं कि वो बीमार है। ये distinction क़रीब दो मिनट में मायने रखने वाला है।
Pathogen वो organism है जो disease cause करता है। नुक़सान वही कर रहा है। जब सवाल कहे 'name the causative organism', तो वो pathogen माँग रहा है, और इस board पर बाक़ी कुछ भी acceptable answer नहीं है।

और vector वो organism है जो pathogen को transport करता है — और उसे ख़ुद कोई disease नहीं होती। वो आख़िरी clause ही इस word का पूरा content है। उसे हटा दीजिए तो vector का मतलब सिर्फ़ pathogen रह जाएगा।

ये रहा triangle। ऊपर pathogen red में क्योंकि नुक़सान वही करता है। नीचे बाएँ host, यानी हम। नीचे दाएँ vector green में, और नीचे से एक dashed arrow जाता हुआ — क्योंकि vector का पूरा काम वही arrow है, pathogen को बीमार इंसान से healthy इंसान तक पहुँचाना।

इसे ऐसे सोचिए। Festival rush में Indian railway network की कल्पना कीजिए। Pathogen वो troublemaker है जिसे किसी दूर के town तक पहुँचना है। कभी-कभी troublemaker सीधे ख़ुद चलकर आ जाता है — आपने cough droplet साँस में ले लिया और pathogen ने अपना सफ़र ख़ुद कर लिया। किसी मदद की ज़रूरत नहीं।

लेकिन कभी-कभी वो अकेले सफ़र नहीं कर सकता और उसे carrier चाहिए — एक train, एक ticket, एक courier। वही courier vector है: एक organism, अक्सर कोई insect, जो ख़ुद disease cause नहीं करता लेकिन pathogen को बीमार इंसान से healthy इंसान तक ferry कर देता है। ये transport है, बस इतना ही।

<whisper>और classic vector है female Anopheles mosquito। वो malaria carry करती है — लेकिन उसे malaria उस sense में नहीं है जिस sense में हमें होता है। वो एक healthy courier है। जब exam पूछे कि mosquito pathogen है या vector, तो यही distinction test हो रहा है, और ये हर साल एक mark का होता है।

sections.title: Two traps hiding inside the 'war' picture

board_events.text: The invasion story is useful — and it misleads in exactly two places
TRAP 1: not every microbe is a pathogen. Your gut teems with harmless and even helpful bacteria.
The label 'pathogen' applies ONLY when harm results. It is a verdict, not a taxonomy.

board_events.caption: Not every microbe is a pathogen; and the carrier who spreads while looking well

board_events.text: TRAP 2: a person can carry and spread a pathogen without looking sick at all.
'Typhoid Mary' — Mary Mallon, a cook — infected many people while remaining apparently healthy. A CARRIER.
So 'no symptoms' does NOT mean 'no infection'.
This carrier state is exactly why PUBLIC hygiene matters, and not just personal hygiene.

segments.text: The walled-city picture is genuinely useful and I am going to keep using it. But two traps hide inside it, and both of them come from taking the war metaphor too literally.

Trap one. Not every microbe is a pathogen. Your gut teems with harmless and even helpful bacteria right now, in enormous numbers, and none of them are invaders. If microbe meant enemy, you would be under permanent siege by your own digestive system.

So the label pathogen applies only when harm results. That is worth restating because of how strange it is: pathogen is not a taxonomic category. It is a verdict. The same kind of organism can be harmless in one place and a pathogen in another — what decides it is whether harm follows.
Look at the top panel. Harmless gut flora on one side, Salmonella typhi on the other. Both bacteria. Same kingdom, opposite verdict. Nothing about being a bacterium made the difference.

Trap two, and this one is more dangerous because it breaks the picture at the level of common sense. A person can carry and spread a pathogen without looking sick at all. The city can be occupied and still look like it is doing fine.

The infamous case is Typhoid Mary — Mary Mallon, a cook, who infected many people while remaining apparently healthy herself. She was not lying and she was not being careless. She was a carrier: infected, transmitting, and showing nothing.

So write this one down, because it is the sentence that trap exists to teach. No symptoms does not mean no infection. Being well and being uninfected are two different claims, and only one of them is visible from the outside.

<excited>And now watch how the biology forces the public policy. This carrier state is exactly why public hygiene matters, and not just personal hygiene. If you could tell who was infected by looking, personal caution would be enough — you would simply avoid them. You cannot. So a healthy-looking cook handling food is a public health question, and the community, not the individual, has to answer it.
Walled-city वाली picture सच में काम की है और मैं इसे आगे भी use करूँगा। लेकिन इसके अंदर दो traps छिपे हैं, और दोनों war metaphor को ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा literally लेने से आते हैं।

Trap एक। हर microbe pathogen नहीं होता। आपकी gut में अभी इसी वक़्त harmless और यहाँ तक कि helpful bacteria भारी तादाद में भरे हुए हैं, और उनमें से कोई invader नहीं है। अगर microbe का मतलब दुश्मन होता, तो आप अपने ही digestive system की permanent घेराबंदी में होते।

तो pathogen का label सिर्फ़ तब लगता है जब harm हो। इसे दोहराना ज़रूरी है क्योंकि ये बात कितनी अजीब है: pathogen कोई taxonomic category नहीं है। ये एक verdict है। एक ही तरह का organism एक जगह harmless हो सकता है और दूसरी जगह pathogen — तय ये करता है कि harm हुआ या नहीं।
ऊपर वाला panel देखिए। एक तरफ़ harmless gut flora, दूसरी तरफ़ Salmonella typhi। दोनों bacteria। एक ही kingdom, उल्टा verdict। Bacterium होने से कोई फ़र्क़ नहीं पड़ा।

Trap दो, और ये ज़्यादा ख़तरनाक है क्योंकि ये picture को common sense के level पर तोड़ता है। कोई इंसान pathogen carry और spread कर सकता है और बिल्कुल बीमार न दिखे। City occupied हो सकती है और फिर भी ठीक-ठाक दिख सकती है।

मशहूर case है Typhoid Mary — Mary Mallon, एक cook, जिसने बहुत लोगों को infect किया जबकि ख़ुद apparently healthy बनी रही। वो झूठ नहीं बोल रही थी और लापरवाह भी नहीं थी। वो एक carrier थी: infected, transmitting, और कुछ भी दिखाए बिना।

तो ये लिख लीजिए, क्योंकि यही वो sentence है जिसे सिखाने के लिए ये trap मौजूद है। No symptoms का मतलब no infection नहीं है। Well होना और uninfected होना दो अलग claims हैं, और इनमें से सिर्फ़ एक बाहर से दिखता है।

<excited>और अब देखिए biology कैसे public policy को मजबूर कर देती है। यही carrier state exactly वो वजह है कि public hygiene मायने रखती है, सिर्फ़ personal hygiene नहीं। अगर देखकर पता चल जाता कि कौन infected है, तो personal सावधानी काफ़ी होती — आप बस उससे दूर रहते। पता नहीं चलता। इसलिए healthy दिखने वाली cook का खाना छूना एक public health का सवाल है, और इसका जवाब community को देना है, individual को नहीं।

board_events.text: Which is precisely WHY typhoid spreads through contaminated food and water — rather than through the air.
Common cold: route is the respiratory tract, so transmission is by droplet.
Malaria: route is a mosquito bite, so vector control is what works.
Ringworm: route is direct contact and soil, so hygiene of the surface is the answer.
Transmission is not an arbitrary fact to memorise. It FOLLOWS from where the pathogen can survive.

segments.text: Here is a small idea that quietly does an enormous amount of work, and most students walk past it. A pathogen must adapt to survive inside the host. It does not get to arrive anywhere it likes.

Take the example the chapter gives. A gut pathogen like Salmonella must withstand stomach acid and digestive enzymes to reach the intestine. That is a genuinely hostile journey — the stomach is designed to destroy exactly this kind of thing, and most organisms that go in do not come out the other side.

Look at the top row. Contaminated food and water, then the stomach with its acid and enzymes, then the small intestine, which is the target. Salmonella has to survive the middle box to reach the third one. Not all bacteria can.

And now the payoff, which is why I made you sit through the gauntlet. This is precisely why typhoid spreads through contaminated food and water rather than through the air. Not by convention. Not because a textbook decided so. Salmonella can survive the gut route, so the gut route is how typhoid travels.

Run the same logic across the bottom row and the whole subtopic gets easier. The common cold's route is the respiratory tract — the rhino virus survives there — so transmission is by droplet, and you catch it from someone's cough.

Malaria's route is a mosquito bite, delivered straight into the blood, bypassing every barrier you have. So no amount of hand-washing touches malaria, and vector control is what actually works. The route dictates the countermeasure.

Ringworm's route is direct contact and soil — a fungus on the surface of the skin, never going deeper. So hygiene of the surface is the answer, and it is why the disease lives in skin folds where it is warm and damp.

<excited>So here is the habit I want you to build. Transmission is not an arbitrary fact to memorise alongside the organism's name. It follows from where the pathogen can survive. Learn the route, and the mode of transmission stops being a separate line in the table — you can reconstruct it.

अब एक छोटा idea जो चुपचाप बहुत बड़ा काम करता है, और ज़्यादातर students इसके बग़ल से निकल जाते हैं। Pathogen को host के अंदर survive करने के लिए adapt करना पड़ता है। उसे जहाँ मन करे वहाँ पहुँचने की छूट नहीं है।

Chapter का example लीजिए। Salmonella जैसे gut pathogen को intestine तक पहुँचने के लिए stomach acid और digestive enzymes झेलने पड़ते हैं। ये सचमुच का hostile सफ़र है — stomach बना ही इसी तरह की चीज़ को ख़त्म करने के लिए है, और जो organisms अंदर जाते हैं उनमें से ज़्यादातर दूसरी तरफ़ नहीं निकलते।

ऊपर वाली row देखिए। Contaminated food और water, फिर stomach अपने acid और enzymes के साथ, फिर small intestine जो target है। Salmonella को तीसरे box तक पहुँचने के लिए बीच वाला box survive करना है। हर bacterium ये नहीं कर सकता।

और अब payoff, जिसके लिए मैंने आपको ये पूरा gauntlet दिखाया। यही exactly वो वजह है कि typhoid contaminated food और water से फैलती है, हवा से नहीं। किसी convention की वजह से नहीं। इसलिए नहीं कि textbook ने तय कर दिया। Salmonella gut route survive कर सकता है, इसलिए typhoid gut route से ही चलता है।

यही logic नीचे वाली row पर चलाइए और पूरा subtopic आसान हो जाएगा। Common cold का route respiratory tract है — rhino virus वहाँ survive करता है — इसलिए transmission droplet से होता है, और आपको ये किसी की खाँसी से लगती है।

Malaria का route mosquito bite है, सीधे blood में delivered, आपकी हर barrier को bypass करते हुए। इसलिए कितना भी हाथ धो लीजिए, malaria को फ़र्क़ नहीं पड़ता, और असल में काम vector control करता है। Route ही countermeasure तय करता है।
Ringworm का route direct contact और soil है — skin की सतह पर एक fungus, कभी गहरा नहीं जाता। इसलिए जवाब है सतह की hygiene, और इसीलिए ये disease skin folds में बसती है जहाँ गर्मी और नमी रहती है।

<excited>तो ये आदत बनाइए। Transmission कोई arbitrary fact नहीं है जिसे organism के नाम के साथ रट लिया जाए। ये इस बात से निकलता है कि pathogen कहाँ survive कर सकता है। Route सीख लीजिए, और mode of transmission table की अलग line होना बंद कर देगा — आप उसे ख़ुद reconstruct कर लेंगे।

sections.title: Bacterial diseases I: typhoid and pneumonia

Sustained high fever (39-40 C), weakness, stomach pain, constipation, headache. Severe: intestinal perforation.
Transmission: contaminated food and water, to the intestine, then the blood. The WIDAL test confirms.

board_events.text: PNEUMONIA — Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae — the ALVEOLI of the lungs.
Fever, chills, cough, headache. Severe: lips and nail-beds turn grey-to-bluish.
Transmission: inhaling droplets or aerosols; also sharing utensils with an infected person.
Typhoid = food and water. NEVER air. That swap is a standard MCQ trap.

segments.text: Now the tables. The single most exam-tested thing in this chapter is the disease-to-pathogen-to-transmission-to-symptom grid, and I want to say something about how you store it. Learn it as a grid. Not as a paragraph, not as a story — as rows and columns, because that is how it is examined.

Typhoid first. Causative organism: Salmonella typhi, a bacterium. Tissue affected: the small intestine. Small — hold that word, because there is another gut disease coming that takes the large intestine, and telling them apart is worth a mark.

Symptoms: a sustained high fever, thirty nine to forty degrees Celsius, with weakness, stomach pain, constipation and headache. Note constipation specifically — this is not a bloody-diarrhoea disease, and that will matter shortly. In severe cases, intestinal perforation.

Transmission: contaminated food and water, into the intestine, then spreading through the blood. And the confirmatory test — this is a guaranteed question — is the Widal test. Salmonella typhi, Widal test. Say those two together enough times that one pulls up the other.

Here is the grid. Four columns: disease, organism, what it affects, how it travels and how it is confirmed. Every bacterial disease in this chapter is one row of exactly this shape, and when a match-the-column question arrives, you are just reading a row back.

Second row: pneumonia. Two causative organisms, and the exam expects both — Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. Tissue affected: the alveoli of the lungs. The alveoli, specifically, where gas exchange happens. Underline that, because the contrast with the common cold is built on it.

Symptoms: fever, chills, cough, headache. And in severe cases a sign worth remembering because it is so visual — the lips and nail-beds turn grey to bluish. Ask yourself why. The alveoli are where oxygen enters the blood; damage them and oxygenation drops, and the colour change is that failure showing at the surface.

Transmission for pneumonia: inhaling droplets or aerosols. And a second route the chapter names explicitly and students forget — sharing utensils with an infected person. That one turns up in questions precisely because it is the one nobody revises.

<whisper>And one warning before we move. Typhoid is food and water. Never air. There is an M C Q, and it runs almost every year, offering you 'typhoid, Salmonella typhi, inspired air'. The organism is right. The disease is right. The route is wrong, and the option is wrong. They are testing the column you did not check.

अब tables। इस chapter में सबसे ज़्यादा exam होने वाली चीज़ है disease-to-pathogen-to-transmission-to-symptom grid, और मैं ये कहना चाहता हूँ कि इसे store कैसे करें। इसे grid की तरह सीखिए। Paragraph की तरह नहीं, कहानी की तरह नहीं — rows और columns की तरह, क्योंकि exam इसी तरह होता है।

पहले typhoid। Causative organism: Salmonella typhi, एक bacterium। Tissue affected: small intestine। Small — इस शब्द को पकड़िए, क्योंकि आगे एक और gut disease आ रही है जो large intestine लेती है, और इन दोनों में फ़र्क़ करना एक mark का है।

Symptoms: sustained high fever, उनतालीस से चालीस degrees Celsius, साथ में weakness, stomach pain, constipation और headache। Constipation पर ख़ास ध्यान दीजिए — ये bloody-diarrhoea वाली disease नहीं है, और ये थोड़ी देर में काम आएगा। Severe cases में intestinal perforation।

Transmission: contaminated food और water, intestine में, फिर blood के ज़रिए फैलाव। और confirmatory test — ये guaranteed सवाल है — Widal test है। Salmonella typhi, Widal test। इन दोनों को इतनी बार साथ बोलिए कि एक दूसरे को अपने आप खींच लाए।

ये रहा grid। चार columns: disease, organism, किसे affect करती है, कैसे चलती है और कैसे confirm होती है। इस chapter की हर bacterial disease बिल्कुल इसी shape की एक row है, और जब match-the-column आएगा, तो आप बस एक row वापस पढ़ रहे होंगे।

दूसरी row: pneumonia। दो causative organisms, और exam दोनों माँगता है — Streptococcus pneumoniae और Haemophilus influenzae। Tissue affected: फेफड़ों की alveoli। Alveoli, specifically, जहाँ gas exchange होता है। इसे underline कीजिए, क्योंकि common cold से इसका contrast इसी पर बना है।

Symptoms: fever, chills, cough, headache। और severe cases में एक sign जो याद रखने लायक़ है क्योंकि वो इतना visual है — lips और nail-beds grey से bluish हो जाते हैं। ख़ुद से पूछिए क्यों। Alveoli वहीं हैं जहाँ oxygen blood में जाता है; उन्हें damage कीजिए तो oxygenation गिरता है, और वो colour change उसी failure का सतह पर दिखना है।

Pneumonia का transmission: droplets या aerosols साँस में लेना। और एक दूसरा route जो chapter explicitly बताता है और students भूल जाते हैं — infected person के साथ utensils share करना। वो सवालों में exactly इसीलिए आता है क्योंकि उसे कोई revise नहीं करता।

<whisper>और आगे बढ़ने से पहले एक चेतावनी। Typhoid food और water है। कभी air नहीं। एक M C Q है, और वो लगभग हर साल आता है, जो आपको देता है 'typhoid, Salmonella typhi, inspired air'। Organism सही। Disease सही। Route ग़लत, और option ग़लत। वो उसी column का exam ले रहे हैं जो आपने check नहीं किया।

sections.title: Bacterial diseases II — and the chapter's only virus

PLAGUE — Yersinia pestis — the 'Black Death'. Vector: the rat-flea.
DIPHTHERIA — Corynebacterium diphtheriae — upper respiratory mucosa. Symptom: difficulty breathing. Respiratory route.

board_events.text: COMMON COLD — rhino viruses — the nose and respiratory passage. NOT the lungs.
Nasal congestion and discharge, sore throat, hoarseness, cough, headache. Lasts 3-7 days.
Cold = viral, nose and passage. Pneumonia = bacterial, alveoli.
Don't let the word 'respiratory' blur them. Same tract, different tenant, different depth.
Plague sounds medieval and viral. It is neither — Yersinia pestis is a bacterium.

segments.text: Two more bacterial rows, and then the only viral disease in this subtopic — which turns out to be the one they build the most traps around.

Plague. Yersinia pestis, and it is the Black Death — the disease that emptied medieval Europe. The chapter gives it briefly, and the vector is the rat-flea, so the chain runs rat, to flea, to human. That vector is what makes plague a question rather than a footnote.

Diphtheria. Corynebacterium diphtheriae. It affects the upper respiratory mucosa, the symptom given is difficulty breathing, and the route is respiratory. Short row, easy marks — organism, site, symptom, route, four items and you are done.
Look at the board. Two bacteria at the top, and then the pink panel at the bottom for the cold — and I have separated them physically because everything in that panel behaves differently.

The common cold. Causative organism: rhino viruses, plural, and viral not bacterial. It affects the nose and respiratory passage — and the chapter says something explicitly here that you must not lose. Not the lungs. The virus does not reach the alveoli. It stops in the upper passage.

Symptoms follow directly from that: nasal congestion and discharge, sore throat, hoarseness, cough, headache. Every one of those is an upper-passage symptom. And it lasts three to seven days — a self-limiting illness, which is another thing that separates it from pneumonia.

So hold the pair together, because they are examined as a pair. Cold: viral, nose and passage. Pneumonia: bacterial, alveoli. Different kingdom of pathogen, different depth in the same tract, different severity, different treatment.

Do not let the word respiratory blur them. Both are respiratory diseases and that word is doing nothing to help you — same tract, different tenant, different depth. The M C Q that offers you 'common cold, typhoid, pneumonia' as an all-bacterial set is built exactly on this blur: cold and pneumonia both hit the airway, so the viral one slips through unnoticed.

<chuckle>And one small warning about plague, because the name does the damage. It sounds medieval, it sounds apocalyptic, and it sounds viral. It is none of those things. Yersinia pestis is a bacterium, and in a which-set-is-entirely-bacterial question, plague is quietly correct while everyone stares at it suspiciously.
दो और bacterial rows, और फिर इस subtopic की इकलौती viral disease — जो असल में वही निकलती है जिसके इर्द-गिर्द सबसे ज़्यादा traps बनते हैं।

Plague। Yersinia pestis, और यही Black Death है — वो disease जिसने medieval Europe ख़ाली कर दिया था। Chapter इसे संक्षेप में देता है, और vector है rat-flea, तो chain चलती है चूहा, फिर flea, फिर इंसान। वही vector plague को footnote से सवाल बना देता है।

Diphtheria। Corynebacterium diphtheriae। ये upper respiratory mucosa को affect करती है, symptom दिया है difficulty breathing, और route respiratory है। छोटी row, आसान marks — organism, site, symptom, route, चार items और काम ख़त्म।
Board देखिए। ऊपर दो bacteria, और नीचे cold के लिए pink panel — और मैंने इन्हें physically अलग रखा है क्योंकि उस panel की हर चीज़ अलग तरह से behave करती है।

Common cold। Causative organism: rhino viruses, बहुवचन में, और viral है bacterial नहीं। ये nose और respiratory passage को affect करती है — और chapter यहाँ explicitly एक बात कहता है जिसे खोना नहीं है। फेफड़े नहीं। Virus alveoli तक पहुँचता ही नहीं। वो ऊपरी passage में ही रुक जाता है।

Symptoms सीधे इसी से निकलते हैं: nasal congestion और discharge, sore throat, hoarseness, cough, headache। इनमें से हर एक upper-passage का symptom है। और ये तीन से सात दिन चलती है — एक self-limiting illness, जो एक और चीज़ है जो इसे pneumonia से अलग करती है।

तो इस जोड़ी को साथ पकड़िए, क्योंकि exam इन्हें जोड़ी में ही लेता है। Cold: viral, nose और passage। Pneumonia: bacterial, alveoli। Pathogen का अलग kingdom, एक ही tract में अलग गहराई, अलग severity, अलग इलाज।

Respiratory शब्द को इन्हें धुँधला मत करने दीजिए। दोनों respiratory diseases हैं और वो शब्द आपकी कोई मदद नहीं कर रहा — एक ही tract, अलग किराएदार, अलग गहराई। जो M C Q आपको 'common cold, typhoid, pneumonia' को all-bacterial set की तरह देता है, वो exactly इसी धुँधलेपन पर बना है: cold और pneumonia दोनों airway पर लगती हैं, तो viral वाली चुपके से निकल जाती है।

<chuckle>और plague के बारे में एक छोटी चेतावनी, क्योंकि नुक़सान नाम कर रहा है। ये medieval लगता है, apocalyptic लगता है, और viral लगता है। ये इनमें से कुछ नहीं है। Yersinia pestis एक bacterium है, और which-set-is-entirely-bacterial वाले सवाल में plague चुपचाप सही होती है जबकि सब उसे शक़ से घूरते रहते हैं।

sections.title: Protozoan diseases: malaria and amoebiasis

board_events.text: Two protozoan diseases — and both have a vector story
MALARIA — Plasmodium (vivax, malariae, falciparum, ovale) — vector: the female Anopheles mosquito.
Affects RBCs and liver. Symptoms: recurring chills and high fever.
P. falciparum causes the MALIGNANT, sometimes fatal form.

board_events.text: AMOEBIASIS (amoebic dysentery) — Entamoeba histolytica — vector: houseflies (mechanical).
Affects the LARGE intestine. Constipation, abdominal pain and cramps, stools with excess mucus and blood clots.
Typhoid: SMALL intestine, constipation, sustained fever. Amoebiasis: LARGE intestine, bloody mucus stools.
The housefly is a MECHANICAL carrier — it ferries on its body. The pathogen does not develop inside it.

segments.text: Protozoan diseases now — two of them, and they are two of the highest-yield rows in the chapter. Both have a vector story, and the vectors are completely different animals doing completely different jobs.

Malaria. Causative organism: Plasmodium — and the chapter names four species, so name them: vivax, malariae, falciparum and ovale. Vector: the female Anopheles mosquito. Female. Only the female bites, because she needs a blood meal for her eggs, and any option naming a male vector is wrong by reflex.

It affects the red blood cells and the liver — both, and in that order in the life cycle we are coming to. Symptoms: recurring chills and high fever. Recurring is the word doing work there. Not constant fever. Fever that comes in waves, and in the mechanism section you will see exactly what is producing those waves.

And one species carries a warning label. Plasmodium falciparum causes the malignant, sometimes fatal form. If a question says malignant malaria, or fatal malaria, it is naming falciparum and nothing else. That is a direct match-the-column pair.

Here is the grid for both. Same columns as the bacteria, plus one: vector. And you can already see the contrast being set up in that last column — R B Cs and liver against large intestine. Same kingdom of pathogen, completely different destination.

Amoebiasis, also called amoebic dysentery. Entamoeba histolytica. And the vector here is the housefly — but note the word in brackets: mechanical. Come back to that in a second, because it is a real distinction.

It affects the large intestine — large, and that is the contrast I promised you two sections ago. Symptoms: constipation, abdominal pain and cramps, and the signature — stools with excess mucus and blood clots. That mucus and blood picture is the thing that identifies amoebiasis in a symptom-based question, and it belongs to no other disease in this chapter.

So lock the gut pair together. Typhoid: small intestine, constipation, sustained fever, Widal test. Amoebiasis: large intestine, bloody mucus stools, cramps. When an exam gives you a patient with mucus and blood in the stool and asks for the disease and organ, both halves of the answer come from this contrast.

<curious>And that word mechanical, since I promised. The housefly is a mechanical carrier — it ferries Entamoeba on its body and its feet, from filth to your food. The parasite does not develop inside the fly, and the fly is not part of its life cycle. Compare that with Anopheles, where the mosquito is a genuine host and half the life cycle happens inside her. Both are vectors. Only one is biologically involved.
अब protozoan diseases — दो हैं, और ये chapter की सबसे high-yield rows में से हैं। दोनों की एक vector story है, और vectors बिल्कुल अलग जानवर हैं जो बिल्कुल अलग काम कर रहे हैं।

Malaria। Causative organism: Plasmodium — और chapter चार species गिनाता है, तो गिनिए: vivax, malariae, falciparum और ovale। Vector: female Anopheles mosquito। Female। सिर्फ़ मादा काटती है, क्योंकि उसे अपने अंडों के लिए blood meal चाहिए, और male vector बताने वाला कोई भी option reflex से ग़लत है।

ये red blood cells और liver को affect करती है — दोनों को, और जिस life cycle पर हम आ रहे हैं उसमें इसी क्रम में। Symptoms: recurring chills और high fever। Recurring वो शब्द है जो यहाँ काम कर रहा है। लगातार बुखार नहीं। बुखार जो लहरों में आता है, और mechanism वाले section में आप देखेंगे कि वो लहरें बना क्या रहा है।

और एक species पर चेतावनी का लेबल लगा है। Plasmodium falciparum malignant, कभी-कभी fatal form करती है। अगर सवाल कहे malignant malaria, या fatal malaria, तो वो falciparum का नाम ले रहा है और किसी का नहीं। ये सीधा match-the-column का जोड़ा है।

ये रहा दोनों का grid। Bacteria वाले वही columns, प्लस एक: vector। और आख़िरी column में आपको contrast बनता दिख भी रहा है — R B Cs और liver बनाम large intestine। Pathogen का एक ही kingdom, बिल्कुल अलग मंज़िल।

Amoebiasis, जिसे amoebic dysentery भी कहते हैं। Entamoeba histolytica। और यहाँ vector है housefly — लेकिन bracket वाला शब्द देखिए: mechanical। एक second में इस पर लौटता हूँ, क्योंकि ये असली distinction है।

ये large intestine को affect करती है — large, और यही वो contrast है जिसका वादा मैंने दो section पहले किया था। Symptoms: constipation, abdominal pain और cramps, और signature — stools with excess mucus and blood clots। Mucus और blood वाली ये तस्वीर ही symptom-based सवाल में amoebiasis को पहचानती है, और इस chapter की किसी और disease की नहीं है।

तो gut वाली जोड़ी साथ lock कीजिए। Typhoid: small intestine, constipation, sustained fever, Widal test। Amoebiasis: large intestine, bloody mucus stools, cramps। जब exam आपको mucus और blood वाला patient देकर disease तथा organ पूछे, तो answer के दोनों halves इसी contrast से आते हैं।

<curious>और वो शब्द mechanical, क्योंकि वादा किया था। Housefly एक mechanical carrier है — वो Entamoeba को अपने शरीर और पैरों पर ढोकर गंदगी से आपके खाने तक लाती है। Parasite मक्खी के अंदर develop नहीं होता, और मक्खी उसकी life cycle का हिस्सा नहीं है। इसकी तुलना Anopheles से कीजिए, जहाँ mosquito एक असली host है और आधी life cycle उसी के अंदर होती है। दोनों vectors हैं। Biologically शामिल सिर्फ़ एक है।

ASCARIASIS — Ascaris lumbricoides, the roundworm. No vector: contaminated food, water and soil.
Affects the INTESTINE — not the liver. Internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anaemia, intestinal blockage.

board_events.text: FILARIASIS (elephantiasis) — Wuchereria bancrofti and W. malayi — vector: the female Culex mosquito.
Affects the LYMPHATIC VESSELS.
Chronic inflammation of the lymphatic vessels leads to gross deformity of the limbs and genitals.
Anopheles gives malaria. Culex gives filariasis. Two mosquitoes, two entirely different diseases.
Ascariasis affects the INTESTINE. 'Worm plus liver' is a planted wrong option that catches students who only register 'worm'.

segments.text: Helminthic diseases — worms. Two rows, and they end in wildly different places, which is what makes them easy to hold apart once you see it.

Ascariasis. The organism is Ascaris lumbricoides, the common roundworm. And notice the vector column: there isn't one. No insect is involved. It comes through contaminated food, water and soil — the same gut route as typhoid, a completely different kingdom of pathogen.

It affects the intestine. Intestine — and I am going to say that twice, because there is a wrong option built specifically on this. Symptoms: internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anaemia, and intestinal blockage. The anaemia and the bleeding make sense together — the worm is feeding, and you are what it is feeding on.

Look at the two rows and notice the vector column and the tissue column doing all the work. One has no vector and stays in the gut. The other has a mosquito and ends up somewhere you would never guess from the word worm.

Filariasis, also called elephantiasis. Two organisms, and the exam wants both: Wuchereria bancrofti and W. malayi. Vector: the female Culex mosquito. Culex. Not Anopheles. This is one of the highest-frequency confusions in the chapter and we will grid it properly in the next section.

And the tissue is the surprise. Filariasis affects the lymphatic vessels. Not the gut, not the blood, not the muscle — the lymphatic system. That is a completely different body compartment from anything else in this subtopic, and it is why the disease looks the way it does.

Because here is the mechanism in one line: chronic inflammation of the lymphatic vessels leads to gross deformity of the limbs and genitals. Block the lymphatic drainage, keep it blocked for years, and fluid accumulates until the limb swells to the shape that gave the disease its common name. The deformity is not the worm. It is the drainage failing.

So the pair to lock: Anopheles gives malaria, Culex gives filariasis. Two mosquitoes, two entirely different diseases, and the parasites are not even in the same kingdom — Plasmodium is a protozoan, Wuchereria is a helminth.

<whisper>And one planted option to know by sight. Ascariasis affects the intestine. There is a distractor that reads 'ascariasis, liver' and it catches students who only register 'worm plus somewhere in the abdomen' and stop reading. The worm is in the intestine. Not the liver. Read the whole option.
Helminthic diseases — कीड़े। दो rows, और ये बहुत अलग जगहों पर ख़त्म होती हैं, और यही चीज़ इन्हें अलग रखना आसान बना देती है, एक बार दिख जाए तो।

Ascariasis। Organism है Ascaris lumbricoides, आम roundworm। और vector column देखिए: है ही नहीं। कोई insect शामिल नहीं। ये contaminated food, water और soil से आती है — typhoid वाला ही gut route, pathogen का बिल्कुल अलग kingdom।

ये intestine को affect करती है। Intestine — और मैं ये दो बार कहूँगा, क्योंकि इसी पर एक ग़लत option बना हुआ है। Symptoms: internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anaemia, और intestinal blockage। Anaemia और bleeding साथ में समझ आते हैं — worm खा रहा है, और जिसे खा रहा है वो आप हैं।

दोनों rows देखिए और ध्यान दीजिए कि सारा काम vector column और tissue column कर रहे हैं। एक का कोई vector नहीं और वो gut में ही रहती है। दूसरी के पास mosquito है और वो वहाँ पहुँचती है जिसका worm शब्द से अंदाज़ा भी नहीं लगेगा।

Filariasis, जिसे elephantiasis भी कहते हैं। दो organisms, और exam दोनों माँगता है: Wuchereria bancrofti और W. malayi। Vector: female Culex mosquito। Culex। Anopheles नहीं। ये chapter की सबसे ज़्यादा होने वाली उलझनों में से है और अगले section में हम इसे ठीक से grid करेंगे।

और tissue ही असली surprise है। Filariasis lymphatic vessels को affect करती है। Gut नहीं, blood नहीं, muscle नहीं — lymphatic system। ये इस subtopic की किसी भी और चीज़ से बिल्कुल अलग body compartment है, और इसीलिए ये disease वैसी दिखती है जैसी दिखती है।

क्योंकि mechanism एक line में यही है: lymphatic vessels की chronic inflammation limbs और genitals की gross deformity तक ले जाती है। Lymphatic drainage रोक दीजिए, सालों तक रुकी रहने दीजिए, और fluid जमा होता जाता है जब तक limb उस आकार तक न सूज जाए जिससे disease को उसका आम नाम मिला। Deformity worm नहीं है। वो drainage का fail होना है।

तो जोड़ी lock कीजिए: Anopheles देता है malaria, Culex देता है filariasis। दो mosquitoes, दो बिल्कुल अलग diseases, और parasites तो एक ही kingdom के भी नहीं हैं — Plasmodium protozoan है, Wuchereria helminth।

<whisper>और एक planted option देखते ही पहचान लीजिए। Ascariasis intestine को affect करती है। एक distractor है जो लिखता है 'ascariasis, liver' और वो उन students को पकड़ता है जो सिर्फ़ 'worm plus पेट में कहीं' register करके पढ़ना बंद कर देते हैं। Worm intestine में है। Liver में नहीं। पूरा option पढ़िए।

RINGWORM — Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton. Three genera, one disease. Kingdom: Fungi.
Affects skin, nails and scalp. Dry, scaly lesions with intense itching.
Thrives in heat and moisture — hence the skin folds.

<text x="46" y="138" font-size="11" fill="#64748b">— hence the skin folds</text>
<text x="250" y="118" font-size="11.5" fill="#64748b">Three genera, one disease — all three are named</text>
<text x="250" y="138" font-size="11.5" fill="#64748b">in the exam-tested list. Kingdom: Fungi.</text>
<text x="320" y="176" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#dc2626">The female mosquito grid — high-frequency trap</text>

<text x="300" y="240" font-size="12.5" fill="#1f2933">Malaria (Plasmodium) — protozoan</text>
